name: maybe_Os_RefreshCachedHandle
summary: Refreshes a cached kernel handle: queries the fixed IPC session (command 0x0C) for a new handle/status pair, closes the handle currently stored in *handleOut with svc 0x23, and stores the queried value there. It is a handle swap, not a counter read.
evidence: Callee Os_IpcQueryCommand0C (0.50) writes the second reply word to *out and returns the first; the body then closes *handleOut before overwriting it. Nothing in the body reads a timer/counter and no caller (Os_PerfSample_Loop, Fs_ReadRecordWithRetry) uses the value as time, so the old 'Timer' prefix was unsupported; what object command 0x0C returns is still unknown, hence maybe_.

name: maybe_Video_IdctSubblocks
summary: Fragment inside the video block decoder: runs Video_IdctBlock4x4 once for each set bit (1, 2, 4, 8) of the current sub-block mask byte, i.e. reconstructs up to four 4x4 sub-blocks selected by that mask. The mask byte is read through the fixed table address 0x08010400 and the register r6 is an incoming value, so this is a mid-function entry, not a stand-alone API.
evidence: Callee Video_IdctBlock4x4 is now named and the four guarded calls line up exactly with the four mask bits; the twin at 0x0013BCD4 has the same body with its own IDCT copy. The body still shows unaff_r6 (damaged decompilation) and there is no caller of its own, so the description is kept as a maybe_ note instead of being promoted.

name: maybe_Video_IdctSubblocks_B
summary: Second copy of the per-mask 4x4 inverse-transform loop: runs Video_IdctBlock4x4_B once for each set bit (1, 2, 4, 8) of the current sub-block mask byte. Template copy of 0x001356D4 with relocated constants (the two bodies differ in 2 of 84 bytes), entered mid-function.
evidence: Byte-compared with 0x001356D4: identical decompiled body, only the IDCT callee and the constant table address differ. No caller and unaff_r6 (damaged decompilation), so it stays a maybe_ description rather than a promoted entry point.

name: Script_Native_NewSlot
summary: Squirrel native closure for the VM's newslot operation: forwards its untouched argument registers to Script_Vm_NewSlot and maps success to 1 (one value on the VM stack) and failure to -1 (error), the native calling convention.
evidence: Disassembly is the 24-byte native shape: push {r4,lr}; bl Script_Vm_NewSlot; cmp r0,#0; movge r0,#1; mvnlt r0,#0. It sits in the 0x00148xxx..0x00166xxx block of Script_Native_* bound natives (compare Script_Native_TokenizeString) and has no direct bl caller, i.e. it is registered by address. The old 'Script_NewSlot' duplicated the VM routine's own name.

name: Script_Native_GetInstanceUserPointer
summary: Squirrel native closure: forwards its arguments untouched to Script_Vm_GetInstanceUserPointer and returns 1 on success or -1 on failure, so the script sees one result value or an error.
evidence: Disassembly: push {r4,lr}; bl Script_Vm_GetInstanceUserPointer; cmp r0,#0; movge r0,#1; mvnlt r0,#0. Same 24-byte bound-native shape and register forwarding as the other Script_Native_* wrappers; no bl caller, so it is table-registered. The callee is confidently named (0.75), which fixes the operation.

name: Script_Native_TableRemoveKey
summary: Squirrel native closure: forwards its arguments untouched to Script_Table_RemoveKey and returns 1 on success or -1 on failure (one value on the VM stack, or an error).
evidence: The 24-byte body is the same push/bl/cmp/movge/mvnlt wrapper as 0x0014B5D8 and calls the confidently named Script_Table_RemoveKey (0.72); the untouched argument registers are the bound-native convention. No bl caller, so it is registered by address; the old 'ApiResultOk2' name hid which table operation it wraps.

name: maybe_SQCommand_Tail
summary: Not an entry point: this is the tail block of the seed-symbol function SQCommand (0x0015179C), which resolves an object through 0x0063F8F0, rebuilds a text page and restores the 0x14C-byte frame. The Thumb scanner split SQCommand here, which is why the listed callees belong to the enclosing routine.
evidence: SQCommand at 0x0015179C is a 1.00-confidence seed symbol with a 2744-byte range that contains this address; the calls Ghidra attributes here (0x001902B4, Text_Page_BuildAtOffset) are part of SQCommand's own body, which also explains the unrelated Party_Member_/Ui_ItemList callees. Renamed so it is not mistaken for a separate 'finish' API.

name: maybe_Gfx_MovieFrame_BuildEntry
signature: u32 maybe_Gfx_MovieFrame_BuildEntry(void* queue, u32 surface, u32 unused)
summary: Called by Gfx_MovieQueue_Push for every newly decoded movie surface: it fills two six-word arrays in the queue's f_0 sub-structure (a scaled value from f_18 * [sub+8] per slot) and advances a wrapping slot index at +0xC against the capacity at +0x8, then returns the value the frame ring stores for that frame.
evidence: Ghidra's halt_baddata() is wrong: the ARM disassembly at 0x00152EA8 is an intact push {r4-r8,lr} body with a six-iteration loop and an mla scale. Its only real caller is the named Gfx_MovieQueue_Push (0x006B95E4), which stores the return in the ring at f_28[tail] and pairs it with 0x0015D4A0. What the six slots represent is not visible, so the name stays maybe_.

name: Script_Native_SetSlotFromStack
summary: Squirrel native closure: forwards its arguments untouched to Script_SetSlotFromStack and returns 0, i.e. it deliberately leaves no result value on the VM stack (the neighbouring natives return 1 for one value).
evidence: Disassembly is the 16-byte native shape: push {r4,lr}; bl Script_SetSlotFromStack; mov r0,#0; pop. Returning 0 is the Squirrel native convention for 'no result', which explains the observed 'return-zero stub'; the callee is named (0.7+). No bl caller, so it is table-registered.

name: Script_Native_GetInstance
summary: Squirrel native closure: forwards its arguments untouched to Script_Vm_GetInstance and returns 1 on success or -1 on failure.
evidence: 92-byte body is the push/bl/cmp/movge/mvnlt wrapper around the confidently named Script_Vm_GetInstance (0.75), sitting directly next to the other Script_Native_* wrappers; no bl caller, so it is registered by address. The old name described a generic result check instead of the instance operation.

name: Event_DispatchHandlerTimeline
summary: Event-command dispatcher for the timeline table: indexes the 8-byte entries at 0x007A6880 by the byte at cmd+4, requires a non-null handler whose stored style byte equals event[2], then calls handler(event, cmd).
evidence: Its only caller is the named Event_TimelineDispatchRange (0.55), which walks a timeline's sorted frame table, so this is the timeline's command table (0x007A6880) rather than the anim action-sequence table (0x007C310C) used by Event_DispatchHandlerByte4 - whose body it copies exactly, including the one-shot guard and style compare. 'Byte4B' was a decoder artefact.

name: Script_Native_TableGetSlot
summary: Squirrel native closure: forwards its arguments untouched to Script_Table_GetSlot and returns 1 on success or -1 on failure.
evidence: Same 28-byte push/bl/cmp/movge/mvnlt wrapper as its neighbours and the callee is the named Script_Table_GetSlot (0.6); the untouched argument registers are the bound-native convention. No bl caller, so it is registered by address; the old 'ApiResultOk3' name said nothing about which operation it exposes.

name: Script_Native_Clone
summary: Squirrel native closure: forwards its arguments untouched to Script_Vm_Clone and returns 1 on success or -1 on failure.
evidence: 24-byte bound-native wrapper around the confidently named Script_Vm_Clone (0.85), immediately after the other Script_Native_* wrappers; no bl caller. 'Script_Clone' read as if it were the VM routine itself, so the native suffix was added.

name: maybe_MessageRegistActor_Continuation
summary: Not an entry point: a continuation block of MessageRegistActor (0x00159B7C) that calls the overlay slot-sprite getter Ui_Overlay_ResolveSlotSprite on ctx->f_8->f_48. The Thumb decode starts mid-function, so the callees listed for this address belong to the enclosing routine.
evidence: No caller and no prologue; 0x00159B7C MessageRegistActor is the only user of this address. The body loads ctx+8 then +0x48 before the call, which cannot be a stand-alone 'object from handle' API, so the old wording was misleading and is replaced by the enclosing function's name.

name: Script_Native_PushRootTable
summary: Squirrel native closure: pushes the VM root table with Script_Vm_PushRootTable and always returns 1 (the table is the single value the script receives).
evidence: 88-byte body is that one call plus 'return 1', and the callee is the confident Script_Vm_PushRootTable (0.85); no bl caller, so it is table-registered. The old 'ApiCallNoArgs' wording did not say which table is pushed.

name: Event_Cmd_LevelViewEvent0E
summary: Event-command handler: fetches the current level-view object and, when it exists, sends it event 0x0E through vtable slot +0x38 with two zero arguments. Nothing here is UI.
evidence: Registered as a {handler, style} entry in the event-command table dispatched by Event_DispatchHandlerByte4 (0x0014BCA8), and its callee is the field object getter 0x005E64E0 (maybe_Field_GetTypedObjectByHandle); the handler's (event, cmd) arguments are dropped by Ghidra because the body ignores them. The old 'Ui_DispatchScriptEvent' named the wrong subsystem.

name: maybe_Event_Cmd_LevelViewSlot40
summary: Event-command handler: fetches the same level-view object as 0x0015F0E4 and calls its vtable slot +0x40 with the constant 4. Slot +0x40 may be a state/close call, but its target is unrecovered, so only the call shape is named.
evidence: Caller is the event-command dispatcher Event_DispatchHandlerByte4 and the callee is the field level-view getter, so the object is a field object, not a window - the old 'Ui_CloseWindow' was wrong. The slot +0x40 implementation is not in the readable tree, so the name stays descriptive and maybe_.

name: Script_Native_ToString
summary: Squirrel native closure: converts the top argument with Script_Vm_ToString (sq_tostring) and returns 1, leaving the converted string as the single result value.
evidence: 16-byte body: push/bl Script_Vm_ToString/mov r0,#1/pop, with the argument registers forwarded untouched. The callee is confidently named (0.85, matching sq_tostring), which directly contradicts the first pass's 'SetStackTop'. No bl caller, so it is table-registered.

name: Script_Native_CheckOneParam
summary: Squirrel native closure: calls Script_Vm_CheckParams1 and returns 1 when the one-parameter check passes or -1 when it fails.
evidence: 24-byte push/bl/cmp/movge/mvnlt wrapper around the named Script_Vm_CheckParams1 (0.75); no bl caller, so it is registered by address. The old 'ApiResultCheckE' wording hid that this is the one-parameter arity check.

name: maybe_Battle_CommandSlots_TryDecrement
summary: Tries to step the battle manager's stored command slots back: for each of the four 3-byte slots (id/arg/arg2 at +0xFD/+0x100/+0x103/+0x106) whose id is 5 it decrements the third byte, then validates the result with Battle_CheckUnitCommandCondition(self, 5) and restores all four values when the condition fails.
evidence: The slot offsets and the validation call match Battle_CheckUnitCommandCondition (0x001745E8) exactly - that function reads the same f_fd/f_100/f_103/f_106 ids with the f_ff/f_102/f_105/f_108 params - so this is the battle command-slot state machine, not a UI widget animation. What command id 5 means is not shown, so the name keeps maybe_.

name: Battle_CheckCommandCondition
summary: Evaluates the battle manager's stored command: for command id 2 it answers the fallback flag f_F3, otherwise it asks Battle_CheckUnitsCondition(self, f_106, f_108, f_107) and answers 1 on success or f_F3 when the check fails.
evidence: Read together with Battle_CheckUnitCommandCondition (0x001745E8), the field layout (id f_106, params f_107/f_108) is the same four-slot command block, and the callee is the named Battle_CheckUnitsCondition (0.55). The function returns int, so the Check wording is safe; only what command id 2 means remains open.

name: maybe_Model_IsSpecialState
summary: Unit-model predicate used by Battle_CheckUnitsCondition modes 6/7, which require every unit of each of the four 26-unit groups to return 1: 1 when the model is visible, its f_39D flags (mask 0x56) are clear, and either the part code at +0x74A is 0x54 or the part letter at +0x745 is 'A'/'B'/'C'; 0 otherwise. Template copy of 0x001CA7E4.
evidence: New: the caller Battle_CheckUnitsCondition (0.55) uses it as the per-unit test that all units in a group are in the 'special' state, and Actor_ApplyModelPartCodes cites the same part codes. The word 'special' still stands for the undecoded 0x54/'A'/'B'/'C' combination, so the name keeps maybe_.

name: Map_UpdateGridCallback
summary: Trampoline callback that refreshes the current map-grid level instance with Map_UpdateGridInstance and returns 1 so the caller keeps it registered.
evidence: The callee Map_UpdateGridInstance (0.50) resolves a level's placement record and submits its transform; this 16-byte body is exactly that call plus 'return 1', the per-frame callback shape. There is no direct caller because it is installed as a function pointer.

name: maybe_Container_AddInstanceWithHandle
summary: Inserts an instance into a container table when the table is enabled (f_e0 == 1) or kind < 5: reserves a free slot, stores a generation-wrapped handle from f_e4 (wrapping against the limit at *(u32*)0x007A8B40 + 4), then registers the object with 0x0017C9F8.
evidence: The only caller is the still-unnamed 0x005F4D40 ('tP_'), so the old 'Map' attribution had no support; the body shows the free-slot request, the generation-counter bump with wrap, and the registration call 0x0017C9F8. f_e0 may mean enabled or visible, so no visibility claim is made and the name keeps maybe_.

name: Ui_ReleasePageActors
summary: Releases every non-null page object of a pager: calls Ui_ReleasePageActorSlots once for each of the five pointers at self+0x48..+0x58.
evidence: The whole body is visible and the callee Ui_ReleasePageActorSlots frees the 16 page-actor slots; the caller Ui_DimBackgroundFadeOut tears the pager down. Nothing besides the five releases is touched, so the name is no longer a guess.

name: maybe_Field_SceneObject_Refresh
summary: Lightweight per-frame refresh of a field scene object: advances the animation (0x005E780C), re-applies the actor movement state derived from +0x246 (mode 2 when set) through 0x005E7848, then re-selects the animation entry / resets the animation when the flags at +0x29F and +0xB8 are both set.
evidence: No caller; the named callees are Field_SceneObject_ResetAnimation (0.5) and maybe_Actor_SelectAnimEntry0, which fit a refresh but do not pin down its phase or which flag gates it. 'Refresh' stays a description, so the name keeps maybe_.

name: maybe_Text_BuildLayoutSpanA
signature: void maybe_Text_BuildLayoutSpanA(void* self, const TextEntry* entry, u32 word0, u32 word1)
summary: Text-layout span builder: a 552-byte routine with a push {r4-r8,lr} prologue that fills a stack span record, guarded by style < 7 and a non-empty span, before calling the text layout helpers. Ghidra truncates it after the first call, so only the shape is known.
evidence: The disassembly at 0x0018CEA4 really starts with the ARM push and the style/span guard, but the readable C is a single mis-marked wcslen call - a damaged decompilation. Its twin is 0x0018D24C (same family), so the span-builder wording is kept as a maybe_ description.

name: maybe_Text_BuildLayoutSpanB
signature: void maybe_Text_BuildLayoutSpanB(void* self, const TextEntry* entry, u32 word0, u32 word1)
summary: Second layout-span builder of the text renderer: validates the style id, copies the two span words into a 0x84-byte stack record and fills the layout fields, same family as 0x0018CEA4. The decompiled body is truncated at a mis-marked wcslen call.
evidence: Disassembly shows a 0x84-byte frame with nine saved registers and the same 'style < 7 plus non-empty span' guard as Text_SpanHasContent, which made the old 'ThrowArg' name wrong. The body is still damaged, so the description keeps maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_SetOwnerAndDispatch
summary: Attaches a UI widget to its owner: stores the owner/layout word (owner->f_AC) at self+0x70, makes self+0x6C point at self and dispatches through self->f_4C->f_18. The jumptable at 0x0018F310 is lost, so the rest of the routine is unknown.
evidence: Re-read with the neighbours: there is no free and no list walk, so this is attach/init behaviour, not the 'release the child list' the first pass assumed; the only named callee is the shared UI layout prologue 0x001A6520 (currently drN). Kept maybe_ because the vtable tail is unrecovered.

name: maybe_Ui_UnknownPaneSetupC
summary: Unrecoverable vtable-slot pane setup: only the shared UI layout prologue executes before halt_baddata at 0x002C4950, so nothing about the panes it would create survives in the decompiler output. Deliberately left unnamed.
evidence: The disassembly really stops at a bad instruction and there are no named callers or callees beyond the prologue (0x001A6520, currently drN), so no honest behavioural name exists; this entry is kept only so the address is covered.

name: Ui_FiveChildWindow_Init
summary: Window initialiser that wires five embedded sub-widgets (pointers at +0x384..+0x398, aimed at self+0x80/+0x13C/+0x1F8/+0x2B4/+0x31C) and, for each, calls virtual +8 to attach the owner and +0xC to reset it. What the five widgets display is not visible.
evidence: All five offsets and the attach/reset loop are in the body; no pane names or named callees identify the contents, so the name says only 'five children' and does not claim a list window.

name: Ui_SingleTextPaneWindow_Init
summary: Minimal window initialiser: base ctor, then exactly one text pane named 'txt' bound at the window's base layout id (u16 at self+0x14 shifted into the id's high half), and nothing else.
evidence: The literal at 0x003D6278 resolves to 'txt' in the retail image and the body is the base prologue plus a single virtual +0x34 bind, so the pane name and count are no longer guesses; which screen the window belongs to is still not shown.

name: Ui_TxtLWindow_Init
summary: Minimal window initialiser that binds a single text pane whose name literal at 0x003E9FD8 is 'txt_l' (a left-hand text pane, not a numbered row).
evidence: The literal resolves to 'txt_l' in the retail image and the body is the base prologue plus one virtual +0x34 bind; a single 'txt_l' pane does not identify the screen, so the class stays described by its pane, not by a game screen name.

name: Ui_PagedTextChildWindow_InitPanes
signature: void Ui_PagedTextChildWindow_InitPanes(void* self, int arg2, int arg3, int arg4, int arg5)
summary: InitPanes override for a window that embeds a paged-text child at self+0x70: runs the base prologue and forwards all four arguments to Ui_PagedTextWindow_InitRows on that child; it creates no panes of its own.
evidence: The callee is the confident Ui_PagedTextWindow_InitRows (0x0041DD7C) and the child sits at a fixed +0x70, so this is a thin container. Nothing in the body says 'popup', which the old signature assumed, so the parameter type was corrected.

name: Ui_FourPairTextWindow_InitPanes
summary: Binds eight text panes in one pass: txt_r1..txt_r4 at layout ids base+0..3 and txt_l1..txt_l4 at base+4..7, with no pager or overlays.
evidence: All eight literals resolve (0x00405220..0x00405258) and the body binds exactly those eight ids, so 'four left + four right' is proven; 'ShopWindow' from the first pass was inferred from a neighbouring swap window and is dropped.

name: Ui_TextPaneWindow_Init
summary: Minimal window initialiser that binds the single text pane 'txt' at the window's base layout id.
evidence: The literal at 0x004AAD00 resolves to 'txt' and the body is the base prologue plus one virtual +0x34 bind; a lone 'txt' pane does not identify the screen, so the class is described by its pane only.

name: Ui_TextPaneWindow_Init_776168
summary: Window initialiser of the class with vtable 0x00776168: binds the single text pane 'txt'; Ghidra stops at a jumptable right after the bind, so any further panes are unrecovered.
evidence: The literal at 0x004ADD00 resolves to 'txt' and the fourth argument 0x004ADCFC is an address inside this function's own code range, which shows the decompiler truncated rather than that the function is empty. The class is identified by its vtable address because nothing else distinguishes it.

name: Ui_TextPaneWindow_Init_776E00
summary: Window initialiser of the class with vtable 0x00776E00: binds the single text pane 'txt'; the tail after the bind is lost to a jumptable.
evidence: The literal at 0x004B741C resolves to 'txt', so the first pass's 'no panes' description was wrong - it binds exactly one text pane. The class is still identifiable only by its vtable address.

name: Ui_TextPaneWindow_Init_778C24
summary: Window initialiser of the class with vtable 0x00778C24: binds the single text pane 'txt' before the decompiler loses the jumptable tail.
evidence: The literal at 0x004CF83C resolves to 'txt' and the body is the same one-pane shape as 0x004AACC0, so the name now says what is actually bound; the class stays identified by its vtable address.

name: Ui_TextPaneWindow_Init_77A4BC
summary: Window initialiser of the class with vtable 0x0077A4BC: binds the single text pane 'txt'.
evidence: The literal at 0x004DCECC resolves to 'txt', replacing the first pass's 'no panes' claim, and the body is the one-pane shape; the class remains identified only by its vtable address.

name: Ui_TextPaneWindow_Init_77B64C
summary: Window initialiser of the class with vtable 0x0077B64C: binds the single text pane 'txt'.
evidence: The literal at 0x004E74EC resolves to 'txt', so this is a one-pane text window rather than the empty widget the first pass described; nothing in the body identifies the screen.

name: Ui_PagedTextWindow_InitRowsBase
signature: void Ui_PagedTextWindow_InitRowsBase(void* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4, u32 arg5)
summary: Initialiser for the window whose paged-text child sits at self-0x70: runs the base prologue on self-0x70 and hands the whole layout to Ui_PagedTextWindow_InitRows. The vtable slot is an init, not a destructor.
evidence: The callee is the known Ui_PagedTextWindow_InitRows (0x0041DD7C) and the vtable at 0x0076CD54 holds this entry in an init slot next to Ui_Widget_ReleaseSub/Ui_Pane_SetVisibleWithAnim, so the first pass's 'destructor thunk' reading was wrong. Which window class it belongs to is not shown.

name: maybe_Text_UpdateStyleParams
summary: Rebuilds a text object's style from its cached copy: copies the 16 style words at self+0x8668..+0x86A4 into a local TextStyleBlock, resolves it with Text_ResolveStyleBlock and applies the result to the object through 0x00613F14.
evidence: Both callees are themselves truncated: Text_ResolveStyleBlock ends at a mis-marked wcslen, and 0x00613F14 currently has no symbol of its own (it falls inside ItemBag_SortIdList's address range, which cannot be the real caller). The 16-word cache copy and the two-stage resolve/apply call are clear, so the name stays a maybe_ description.

name: Ui_List_GetSelectedRow
summary: Returns the currently selected row record of a list widget: when the 'has selection' byte at list+0x14 is set it asks vtable slot +0x44 for the cursor index and returns list + index*60 + 0x1B; NULL otherwise.
evidence: The only caller is the named Ui_ShopWindow_HandleConfirmResult (0x00284FD0), which uses the returned pointer as the confirmed row; the 60-byte stride is verified from the index arithmetic. The old 'GetListItem' did not say it returns the selected row, so the name was made specific.

name: maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_ShowSimple
summary: Starts a simple message in a message window: stores the record word in wnd->f_b0->f_136 and sets state 7, style 2 and field 6, then continues into code Ghidra cannot decode. The three callers (Field_ShowSimpleMessage, StatusWindow_UpdateState, LoadDiveMapJump) all use it to show text.
evidence: The visible stores are a fixed message setup and the callers include maybe_Field_ShowSimpleMessage, which supports the show path; the body ends in halt_baddata, so the rest of the setup (and the exact 'simple' semantics) is unknown and the name keeps maybe_.

name: maybe_Gfx_Sprite2D_Refresh
summary: Sprite refresh fragment: the 260-byte Thumb routine is only recovered as a call to the balloon anchor updater (Ui_Balloon_UpdateAnchorPosition, 0x0062AE90) plus 'return 0'; the rest of the body is missing, so what it actually refreshes is unknown.
evidence: No caller and a truncated Thumb body; the only recovered callee is Ui_Balloon_UpdateAnchorPosition, which does not justify naming the whole routine, so the old name is kept as a hypothesis at low confidence.

name: Ui_Widget_SetNamedPaneText
signature: void Ui_Widget_SetNamedPaneText(void* self, u32 paneName, u32 arg3, const u16* text)
summary: Sets the text of one named child pane: when the widget has a layout object (f_30/f_34) and a pane name is given it looks the pane up with Ui_Window_CollectNamedPane and, when a string is given, measures it with wcslen and tail-calls Ui_TextElement_SetString. Used by 57 UI update routines, from equipment and shop lists to the status and number-roll panels.
evidence: Disassembly: guard on [self+0x30]/[self+0x34]/r1, then bl Ui_Window_CollectNamedPane, then wcslen(r3) and 'b Ui_TextElement_SetString' with r3 = (length != 0). The old 'Ui_Node_Finalize' claimed a teardown, but there is no free and no destructor call - this is the shared text setter the whole UI layer calls.

name: Field_LevelWork_InitBlockA
summary: Zero-initialises the 0x3FC4-byte level-work sub-block placed at level record +0x553C: sets the head words, turns the embedded intrusive list heads into self-pointers (f_88=&f_48, f_A0=&f_90, f_E8=&f_A8, ...) and clears the inline byte arrays of 0x60/0x80/0xC0/0x100/0x180/0x280/0x300 bytes.
evidence: Caller Field_Level_InitSpriteSets (0.50) builds the sprite sub-set and sprite set containers and then chains this initialiser at +0x553C and 0x001B3CEC at +0x20, confirming both are the level work's two large initialisers. Which one holds sprite vs actor data is not shown by the code, so A/B stays a positional label.

name: Field_LevelWork_InitBlockB
summary: Zero-initialises the other level-work sub-block (0x27E8 bytes, placed at level record +0x20): the same list-head-plus-inline-array pattern as 0x001AB6F4 with its own offsets (0x80/0x90/0xC0/0x100/0x300 byte arrays at +0x1A/+0x46/+0x77/+0x18B/...).
evidence: Same caller Field_Level_InitSpriteSets places this one at +0x20 and 0x001AB6F4 at +0x553C, so the A/B pair is verified; the contents (sprite vs actor data) are not identifiable from the initialiser, and the summary no longer claims which is 2D or 3D.

name: Gfx_Movie_SamplePairValues
signature: u32 Gfx_Movie_SamplePairValues(void* self, float* out2, int mode)
summary: Samples a two-value track from the movie player: returns 0 when the cached movie mode is 7, otherwise resolves the key through 0x004FF968(&self+0xAB0, mode==2) and 0x004FF4B4, converts the entry's two unsigned values (+0x14/+0x18) to floats into out[0..1], and returns 1 when the key was found.
evidence: The field it tests (f_104C == 7) is the movie-mode byte cached by Gfx_Movie_IsPlayable (0x001B6DE4), and its only caller is Ui_Overlay_UpdateFlash (0x001DB790), which consumes the pair as the overlay's flash values - so 'Overlay' described the caller, not this sampler. The body is complete and both conversions are VFP integer-to-float.
